headline: The Octopus: An Alien on Earth
intro: Read the fascinating science text about octopuses and answer the questions. Practice your present and past tenses!

reading.title: The Octopus: An Alien on Earth
reading.subtitle: A story about strange intelligence

paragraphs.label: A.
paragraphs.text: If you want to see a real alien, you don't need to look at the stars. You just need to look in the ocean. The octopus is one of the strangest animals on our planet. It has three hearts, blue blood, and nine brains. Yes, you read that right! It has one main brain in its head and a small brain in each of its eight arms.

paragraphs.label: B.
paragraphs.text: Last summer, marine biologists studied an octopus in the Pacific Ocean. While the scientists were watching, the octopus changed its color and texture to look exactly like a rock. It hid from a shark that was swimming nearby. When the shark left, the octopus quickly moved away using its arms to walk on the sea floor.

paragraphs.label: C.
paragraphs.text: Scientists have discovered that octopuses are very intelligent. They can open jars, solve puzzles, and even escape from their tanks at night. An octopus once escaped from a lab by squeezing through a tiny hole and sliding across the floor to a bucket of fish. They are truly the masters of survival.
